title: IIT Bombay Suspends Professor's Deanship and Apologises for Statement on Student's Death
excerpt: The institute retracted its earlier characterisation of events before student Sahil Wakode's death and removed Prof. Suryanarayana Doolla as dean, even as the Mumbai Crime Branch takes over the probe.
body:
• IIT Bombay has suspended Professor Suryanarayana Doolla's deanship with immediate effect and formally apologised for its earlier communication about the circumstances of student Sahil Wakode's death, saying it was "inappropriate" to characterise events before an investigation established the facts.
  • The 20-year-old second-year BTech student was found dead in his hostel room on Friday, hours after he was allegedly caught using a mobile phone during a mid-semester examination — the third reported suicide on the campus this year.
  • Doolla, the invigilator during the exam, has been named in a police FIR under abetment-of-suicide and SC/ST Atrocities Act provisions after the student's parents alleged harassment and caste-based discrimination; the Mumbai Crime Branch has taken over the probe.
  • The institute also denied reports that Director Shireesh Kedare had resigned, amid three days of student protests and an 18-point charter of demands calling for an independent inquiry and systemic reforms.

IIT Bombay on Monday suspended the deanship of Professor Suryanarayana Doolla with immediate effect and issued a formal apology retracting its earlier account of the events surrounding the death of 20-year-old student Sahil Wakode, as student protests entered a third day and the Mumbai Crime Branch took over the investigation.

The apology

In a statement released on social media, the institute apologised for the contents of its earlier communication and acknowledged that it had been inappropriate to set out or characterise details relating to the events preceding Wakode's death before they were established through the investigative process. The full text of the apology is quoted below.

The earlier statement, issued September 19, had said Wakode was caught using a mobile phone during the mid-semester examination and had uploaded the question paper to an AI platform to seek answers. It added that he had been counselled and assured the incident would not adversely affect his academic career, and that no disciplinary action had been initiated at that stage. The retraction acknowledges that laying out that narrative before the investigation concluded was wrong.

"We apologise for the statements contained in our earlier communication concerning the circumstances surrounding the unfortunate demise of Sahil... it was inappropriate to have set out or characterised details relating to the events preceding his demise before they had been duly established through the appropriate investigative process."

— IIT Bombay official statement

Suspension of the deanship

Doolla — the invigilator during the September 18 exam and formerly Dean of Student Affairs before taking over as Dean of Administrative Affairs — was removed from the dean's post on the evening of September 20. In an email to students, Director Professor Shireesh Kedare said any further action would follow the investigation. Doolla continues as a professor and head of the Department of Energy Science and Engineering.

The suspension follows sustained protests and an 18-point charter of demands from student representatives: action against Doolla, an independent investigation, reforms to disciplinary procedures, and stronger student welfare and counselling systems. The IIT Bombay Faculty Forum has separately defended Doolla, saying he was performing his invigilator duties and had followed the institute's prescribed, Senate-approved procedures after detecting alleged examination malpractice.

The investigation

Wakode, a second-year BTech student in Energy Science and Engineering, was found dead in his hostel room on Friday, hours after the exam incident — the third reported suicide on campus this year. His parents refused to claim the body at Rajawadi Hospital and demanded a thorough probe. They allege their son was taken out of the examination hall and threatened with suspension, and say he spoke of caste-based discrimination on campus.

On the family's complaint, Mumbai Police registered an FIR under Section 108 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (abetment of suicide) along with provisions of the SC/ST Atrocities Act. Doolla and other officials are named in it. The case has moved from Powai police to the Mumbai Crime Branch. IIT Bombay has denied the discrimination claim; its SC/ST Students and Staff Cell said Wakode had not filed any such complaint with it. The allegations remain under investigation and have not been established.

Why this matters for the diaspora

The IITs are the alma mater of countless engineers and executives abroad. The debate over student welfare, disciplinary fairness, and the use of AI in examinations mirrors conversations on campuses in the US and Europe, where diaspora students navigate similar pressures. How India's most prestigious engineering institute reforms its systems will be watched by its vast global alumni network.

What's next

The Crime Branch investigation will determine the circumstances leading to Wakode's death, including the family's allegations of harassment and discrimination. Students continue to demand an independent inquiry, and the institute faces pressure to act on the 18-point charter beyond the suspension. With three suicides on campus this year, the deeper question — how IIT Bombay protects students within its disciplinary and academic systems — remains unresolved.
